providers.title: A nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone (OpenAI)
providers.scope: p(X,Z,y) = det((det X)Z - Phi_y(adj X)) is hyperbolic with respect to (I,I,0), and no linear matrix inequality of any size describes its closed hyperbolicity cone. Proved in the last lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Degree sixteen (OpenAI)
providers.scope: p/det X is a hyperbolic polynomial of degree 16 with the same cone. Proved in the third lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gårding's theorem
providers.scope: The open hyperbolicity cone is the component of {p != 0} containing e; p is hyperbolic with respect to each of its points; the open and closed cones are convex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Facts on symmetric matrices
providers.scope: Square roots, the variational formula and continuity of the largest eigenvalue, congruence, the Schur complement, kernels, and rI >= C^T C exactly when r >= ||C||^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Determinants of definite pencils
providers.scope: If L(e) > 0, det L(x) is hyperbolic with respect to e and its closed cone is {L(x) >= 0}.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Nonnegativity of the Choi–Lam form
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No dominated bilinear square (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A bilinear form l with l(z,y)^2 <= b(z,y) for all z, y is zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Not a sum of squares
providers.scope: The Choi–Lam form is not a sum of squares of bilinear forms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The positive map Phi_y
providers.scope: u^T Phi_y(vv^T) u = b(v_0 u' - u_0 v', y); hence Phi_y preserves positive semidefiniteness.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hyperbolicity of p (OpenAI)
providers.scope: p is homogeneous of degree 20, p(e) = 1, hyperbolic with respect to e, and p = (det X)^4 det(Z - Phi_y(X^-1)) for invertible X.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two slices of the cone (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For X > 0, (X,Z,y) lies in the cone exactly when Z >= Phi_y(X^-1); (X,Z,0) lies in it exactly when X, Z >= 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A pencil gives a Schur-complement inequality (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A pencil describing the cone yields unital positive maps D, E and a linear B with Z >= Phi_y(X^-1) exactly when E(Z) >= B(y)^T D(X)^-1 B(y).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The norm identity (OpenAI)
providers.scope: b(v_0 u' - u_0 v', y) = ||P(v) B(y) R(u)||^2 for unit u, v, with kernel projections P(v), R(u).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: An exact semidefinite lift (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The cone is the projection of a spectrahedron: there are A_1..A_23, G_1..G_307 in S^100 with x in the cone exactly when sum x_nu A_nu + sum v_j G_j >= 0 for some v. Proved in the last lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Angular Gram factorization (OpenAI)
providers.scope: On the plane y = eta d(t) + xi k, Q(y) = F F^T for an explicit 3x4 matrix F linear in (eta, xi) and trigonometric of degree 3 in t.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectrahedral slices (OpenAI)
providers.scope: p(te - x) = det(tI_20 - L_t(x)) for x on the plane of angle t, so each angular slice of the cone is described by L_t >= 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Degree-two matching (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For S symmetric and z with (z1, z2) != 0 there is C(t) of trigonometric degree 2 with C C^T = Q(z) and <F_t(eta, xi), C(t)>_S = tr(S Q(Y_t(eta, xi), z)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The moment lift (OpenAI)
providers.scope: (X, Z, y) lies in the cone exactly when some linear functional on E satisfies the output equations and H(Lambda) >= 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
